title: Local Vacuum Entanglement through Most Entangled Modes
abstract: We find the shape of the modes containing most of the entanglement between two disjoint spherical regions in the vacuum of a free massless real scalar field in 1+3 Minkowski spacetime. Using the Klco-Beck-Savage method we approximate the field and momentum profile of the vacuum most entangled modes (MEMs) between two spheres. We define a non-perturbative mode-swap entanglement harvesting protocol where two spacelike separated probes extract the maximal amount of entanglement between two regions. Our results are a first step in the direction of understanding the local entanglement structure of quantum fields, pinpointing the exact degrees of freedom that encode accessible quantum correlations in QFT.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the local structure of vacuum entanglement in a free scalar field in Minkowski spacetime. It identifies specific 'Most Entangled Modes' (MEMs) that carry the majority of the distillable entanglement between two separated regions. By proposing a mode-swap protocol and analyzing convergence, the work pinpoints the exact field degrees of freedom responsible for accessible quantum correlations in QFT.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental question of which local field degrees of freedom in Quantum Field Theory (QFT) are responsible for encoding the accessible entanglement between two spatially separated regions in the vacuum.
main_result: The Most Entangled Modes (MEMs) are identified as the dominant carriers of distillable vacuum entanglement, and the entanglement measures (like Logarithmic Negativity) decay exponentially with separation distance.
method: The authors employ the Klco-Beck-Savage method and propose a non-perturbative 'mode-swap entanglement harvesting protocol' to quantify entanglement using the covariance matrix and Logarithmic Negativity.
model_or_system: The study analyzes a free massless real scalar field propagating in 1+3 Minkowski spacetime, focusing on entanglement between two disjoint spherical regions.
key_observables: Logarithmic Negativity (EN), Covariance Matrix ($\sigma$), Mutual Information ($I_{ab}$), and the spatial profiles of the MEMs (field and momentum smearing).
important_parameters: Separation distance ($d$), finite UV cutoff ($N$), and the dimensionality of spacetime (1+3 dimensions).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on restricting the field modes to a finite number $N$ (UV cutoff) and drawing analogies between 1+1 and 1+3 dimensions for convergence analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial profiles of the MEMs for various separations, and plots show the exponential decay of entanglement measures (EN, $I_{ab}$, $	ext{EF}$) with separation distance $d$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the problem of local entanglement structure, developing the MEM concept via the KBS method, quantifying entanglement using $	ext{EN}$, and finally analyzing the convergence properties of these modes in the continuum limit.
why_interesting: The rigorous quantification of vacuum entanglement structure using local field observables and the identification of specific 'entanglement carriers' (MEMs) provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding quantum correlations in QFT, which has implications for quantum information theory in curved or interacting backgrounds.
